response: Yes, early extubation should be the goal for children after congenital cardiac surgery. Most children undergoing congenital heart surgery can be extubated in the operating room, and most neonates can be extubated within the first 24 hours after surgery. Early extubation has been associated with low morbidity rates and short lengths of intensive care unit and hospital stays. This approach can lead to better outcomes and faster recovery for children undergoing congenital cardiac surgery.
